quotes.text: Risk comes from not knowing what you're doing.
quotes.context: Diversification is protection against ignorance. It makes little sense if you know what you're doing. Concentration can actually reduce risk when paired with deep understanding.

quotes.text: All you have to do is mitigate the consequences.
quotes.context: Focus on what you can control — consequences — rather than trying to predict unknowable probabilities. Build systems that gain from disorder rather than merely resisting it.

quotes.text: You've got to have models in your head. And you've got to array your experience — both vicarious and direct — on this latticework of models.
quotes.context: He emphasized inversion ('Invert, always invert') and drawing big ideas from multiple disciplines to avoid 'man with a hammer' syndrome.

quotes.text: The illusion that we understand the past fosters overconfidence in our ability to predict the future.
quotes.context: We are prone to the planning fallacy, over-weighting our own plans while neglecting base rates and luck.

quotes.text: Every decision is risky: it is a commitment of present resources to an uncertain and unknown future.
quotes.context: Every decision commits resources to an unknowable future; the measure of good management is not avoiding risk but making the right risk calculations.

quotes.text: The essence of strategy is choosing what not to do.
quotes.context: Strategy is about making trade-offs and deliberately choosing a different set of activities to deliver unique value. Operational effectiveness is not strategy.

quotes.text: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
quotes.context: If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will also suffer a defeat. If you know neither the enemy nor yourself, you will succumb in every battle.

quotes.text: Strategy without tactics is the slowest route to victory. Tactics without strategy is the noise before defeat.
quotes.context: Vision and execution are inseparable. A plan without practical steps goes nowhere; action without direction is chaos.

quotes.text: All models are wrong, but some are useful.
quotes.context: This is the foundational humility for any modeling work — economic, supply chain, or otherwise. Use models as tools for insight, not as perfect representations of reality.

quotes.text: A system is never the sum of its parts; it's the product of their interaction.
quotes.context: Improving parts in isolation can destroy overall system performance. The best place to solve a problem is often not where it appears.

quotes.text: Management is doing things right; leadership is doing the right things.
quotes.context: Organizations must be built for constant change and to create the future rather than merely predict it.

quotes.text: The best place to solve a problem is often not where it appears.
quotes.context: Effective management focuses on interactions and the whole, not just optimizing individual components or fighting symptoms.

quotes.text: In God we trust; all others bring data.
quotes.context: Decisions must be grounded in evidence, not authority or intuition. If you can't describe what you are doing as a process, you don't know what you're doing.

quotes.role: Engineer & father of the Toyota Production System
quotes.text: Where there is no standard, there can be no kaizen [continuous improvement].
quotes.context: Standards are the baseline for improvement; without them, you're just reacting. Kaizen starts with a clear, repeatable process you can measure and refine.

quotes.role: Physicist & creator of Theory of Constraints
quotes.text: Productivity is the act of bringing a company closer to its goal. Every action that brings a company closer to its goal is productive.
quotes.context: Local optima do not add up to the global optimum — a critical insight for supply chain and complex systems.

quotes.text: Invert, always invert.
quotes.context: Solve problems by thinking backward. Instead of asking 'How do I achieve X?', ask 'What would guarantee failure?' Then avoid those things.

quotes.text: Efficiency is doing things right; effectiveness is doing the right things.
quotes.context: Efficiency optimizes the how; effectiveness questions the what. Both are necessary, but effectiveness comes first.

quotes.text: Some things benefit from shocks; they thrive and grow when exposed to volatility, randomness, disorder, and stressors.
quotes.context: Antifragility is beyond resilience or robustness. The resilient resists shocks and stays the same; the antifragile gets better. Build systems that gain from disorder.

quotes.text: We are prone to the planning fallacy: we make plans based on optimistic scenarios rather than on past experience.
quotes.context: Use an outside view — reference class forecasting — to counter the planning fallacy. Base rates are more reliable than your own story.

quotes.text: Operational effectiveness is not strategy.
quotes.context: Improving operations (benchmarking, TQM, reengineering) is necessary but not sufficient. Strategy requires choosing a unique position that trades off against others.
